title.narrative: Greater Mekong and Subregion (GMS) Southern Coastal Corridor Project

description.narrative: The Project will complete the Greater Mekong Subregion Southern Coastal Corridor (GMS-SCC) in Cambodia and Viet Nam. The Project will include the following components: (i) Rehabilitation of Transport Infrastructure. In Cambodia 15 km of NR33 will be improved to the border with Viet Nam at Preak Chak. In Viet Nam 89.5 km of National Highway (QL) 80 and QL63 will be improved, include construction of two large bridges across the Cai Be and Cai Lon Rivers; (ii) Cross Border Facilities. A new cross border facility will be provided, the design will take into account the ongoing work on the implementation of the GMS Cross-Border Transport Agreement; (iii) HIV/AIDS and trafficking awareness and prevention; and (iv) Road maintenance in Cambodia.

Reduce transport times and costs, and induce more efficient movement of passengers and goods within the project area and between GMS countries

Traffic on improved roads increases by 40% from 2008 baseline within 2 years of project completion Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. The actual traffic of the project corridor in 2018 increased by 117% in comparing with that in 2005 (there is no available baseline traffic number as of 2008 at appraisal of original financing; instead, traffic survey data as of 2005 was used as the baseline) with annual increase rate of 6.1%. Data Source: Field surveys and interviews of road transport operators and road users

Reduction in passenger and freight vehicle operating costs by an average of 30%, in real terms, within 5 years of project completion Achievement: 36 Progress/Status: Achieved. Upon project completion, the unit VOC was reduced by 23% to 36% for different vehicle types by comparing "with-project" and "without-project" cases; IRI reduced from 4-6 at appraisal to 2.3 in 2018; benefits from time savings by having bridges. Data Source: Baseline traffic and transport cost data

Cross-border processing times of under 0.5 hours for passengers and under 2.0 hours for freight by project completion Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Passengers : under 0.5 hour Freights : 1-2 hours Data Source: Traffic counts at border crossings and strategic points in the transport network; customs statistics Base year: 2008 Baseline value: N
